rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi reports that Israfil accompanied Muhammad’s prophethood for three years, teaching him words but not reciting the Quran; Gabriel then accompanied him for twenty years of Quranic revelation.
rows.anchor: عن الشعبي قال أنزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم النبوة وهو ابن أربعين سنة

rows.speaker: ابن عساكر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAsakir says Israfil’s charge over the Trumpet suits a prophethood heralding the Hour’s nearness and end of revelation; he gives comparable angelic assignments to Dhu al-Qarnayn and Khalid ibn Sinan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عساكر والحكمة في توكيل إسرافيل أنه الموكل بالصور

rows.speaker: ابن سابط
rows.claim: Ibn Sabit says three angels preserve what is in the Mother Book: Gabriel handles scriptures, revelation, wartime victory and destructive events; Michael rain and plants; the Angel of Death takes souls, and their records match at resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن ابن سابط قال في أم الكتاب كل شيء هو كائن إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: عطاء بن السائب
rows.claim: ʿAta ibn al-Saʾib says Gabriel is first to be reckoned because he was God’s trustee over His messengers.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء بن السائب قال أول ما يحاسب جبريل لأنه كان أمين الله على رسله

rows.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
rows.claim: Abu Musa recalls a surah like the Musabbihat they used to recite but later forgot, except for a verse warning believers against saying what they do not do.
rows.anchor: عن أبي موسى الأشعري قال كنا نقرأ سورة نشبهها المسبحات

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar says they recited a warning against disowning their fathers as disbelief; Zayd ibn Thabit confirmed the wording when Umar asked him.
rows.anchor: ثم قال لزيد بن ثابت أكذلك قال نعم

rows.speaker: عمر، عبد الرحمن بن عوف
rows.claim: Umar asked ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf about a revealed command to strive as before; ʿAbd al-Rahman said it was among what had been dropped from the Quran.
rows.anchor: قال عمر لعبد الرحمن بن عوف ألم تجد فيما أنزل علينا

rows.speaker: مسلمة بن مخلد الأنصاري
rows.claim: Muslima ibn Mukhallad recited two passages absent from the codex, promising success to believers who emigrated and strove, and hidden delight as reward for those who sheltered, supported and defended them.
rows.anchor: أن مسلمة بن مخلد الأنصاري قال لهم ذات يوم أخبروني بآيتين في القرآن لم يكتبا في المصحف

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that two men who learned a surah from the Prophet could no longer recite a letter; the Prophet said it was among what had been abrogated and to leave it.
rows.anchor: إن ابن عمر قال قرأ رجلان سورة أقرأهما رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that a passage about the Biʾr Maʿuna martyrs was recited until withdrawn: they told their people they had met their Lord, who was pleased with them and whom they pleased.
rows.anchor: وفي الصحيحين عن أنس في قصة أصحاب بئر معونة الذين قتلوا

rows.speaker: حذيفة
rows.claim: Hudhayfa says the portion of the Quran people recite is only a quarter of Surat al-Tawba.
rows.anchor: وفي المستدرك عن حذيفة قال ما تقرءون ربعها يعني براءة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A weak report from Anas says taking adornment at every mosque means praying in sandals; the source notes corroboration from Abu Hurayra.
rows.anchor: عن أنس عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في قوله

rows.speaker: البراء بن عازب
rows.claim: Al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib reports the Prophet’s account of a disbeliever’s soul: heaven’s gates shut, its record placed in Sijjin and it cast down; the Prophet recited verses about the gates and an idolater’s fall.
rows.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ذكر العبد الكافر إذا قبضت روحه

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jabir reports the Prophet identified the people of the Heights as those whose good and bad deeds were equal; the source notes supporting witnesses.
rows.anchor: عن جابر بن عبد الله قال سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عمن استوت حسناته وسيئاته

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن المزني
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Rahman al-Muzani reports the Prophet’s view that they were killed in God’s path while disobeying their parents: one barred Paradise, the other barred Hell; other reports support this.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن المزني قال سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عن أصحاب الأعراف

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: A weak report from Anas, raised to the Prophet, identifies the people of the Heights as believing jinn.
rows.anchor: بسند ضعيف عن أنس مرفوعا انهم مؤمنو الجن

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿAʾisha reports that the Prophet glossed al-tufan as death.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة قالت قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports the Prophet gestured thumb to index fingertip as he recited God’s manifestation to the mountain; the mountain sank and Moses fell unconscious. Al-Hakim and al-Tirmidhi authenticated the report.
rows.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قرأ

rows.speaker: أبو الشيخ
rows.claim: Abu al-Shaykh gives another wording: the Prophet gestured with his little finger, and the mountain was made rubble by its light.
rows.anchor: وأخرجه أبو الشيخ بلفظ ( وأشار بالخنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute over whether people can know the ambiguous verses’ interpretation turns on syntax: the deeply rooted may be joined to God as knowing, or begin a new sentence with “they say” as predicate.
rows.anchor: اختلف هل المتشابه مما يمكن الإطلاع على علمه أو لا يعلمه إلا الله على قولين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through Mujahid, Ibn ʿAbbas says he is among those who know the interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال أنا ممن يعلم تأويله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the deeply rooted know the interpretation and say, “We believe in it.”
rows.anchor: قال يعلمون تأويله ويقولون آمنا به

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak argues they must know the interpretation, or could not distinguish abrogating from abrogated, lawful from unlawful, and clear from ambiguous.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك قال الراسخون في العلم يعلمون تأويله

rows.speaker: النووي
rows.claim: Al-Nawawi prefers that people can know the interpretation: it is unlikely God would address people with something no human could understand.
rows.anchor: واختار هذا القول النووي فقال في شرح مسلم إنه الأصح

rows.speaker: الأكثرون من الصحابة والتابعين وأتباعهم
rows.claim: Most Companions, Successors, followers and later scholars, especially Sunnis, take the other reading: only God knows the interpretation; the author calls this the stronger Ibn ʿAbbas report.
rows.anchor: وأما الأكثرون من الصحابة والتابعين وأتباعهم ومن بعدهم خصوصا أهل السنة فذهبوا إلى الثاني

rows.speaker: ابن السمعاني
rows.claim: Ibn al-Samʿani says only a small group held that the deeply rooted know the interpretation; al-ʿUtbi chose that view despite Sunni doctrine, which Ibn al-Samʿani calls a scholar’s lapse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السمعاني لم يذهب إلى القول الأول إلا شرذمة قليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the majority view, citing a sound Ibn ʿAbbas reading that pauses after “except God” and begins a new statement about the deeply rooted; though not canonical, it securely records his interpretation.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ / وما يعلم تأويله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the verse condemns followers of ambiguity as deviant seekers of discord and praises those who entrust knowledge to God and submit, supporting the majority reading.
rows.anchor: الآية دلت على ذم متبعي المتشابه ووصفهم بالزيغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal noun in “submit fully” is an emphatic cognate accusative; the source groups it with emphatic accusatives for the sky’s surging and mountains’ movement.
rows.anchor: ومن أمثلته ﴿ وسلموا تسليما ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is not emphatic: the form is a plural of suspicion, covering different kinds of suspicion.
rows.anchor: وليس منه ﴿ وتظنون بالله الظنونا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may exemplify this emphasis, or “a thing” may mean an affair or matter.
rows.anchor: وأما ﴿ إلا أن يشاء ربي شيئا ﴾ فتحتمل أن يكون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual emphatic accusative is qualified by an adjective, as in remembering God much and releasing women graciously.
rows.anchor: والأصل في هذا النوع أن ينعت بالوصف المراد نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The qualifying description may instead be attached to the verbal noun, as in fearing God as He deserves.
rows.anchor: وقد يضاف وصفه إليه نحو ﴿ اتقوا الله حق تقاته ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis may use a verbal noun from another verb or a concrete noun instead of a verbal noun: “vegetation” means “growing.”
rows.anchor: وقد يؤكد بمصدر فعل آخر أو اسم عين نيابة عن المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An emphatic circumstantial accusative is another form; examples include “alive,” “doing corruption,” “a messenger,” “turning away” and “not far away.”
rows.anchor: رابعها الحال المؤكدة نحو ﴿ ويوم أبعث حيا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He turned away fleeing” is not emphatic because turning can occur without fleeing; the command to turn one’s face toward the Sacred Mosque shows the difference.
rows.anchor: وليس منه ﴿ ولى مدبرا ﴾ لأن التولية قد لا تكون إدبارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He smiled laughing” is not emphatic because smiling need not be laughter.
rows.anchor: ولا ﴿ فتبسم ضاحكا ﴾ لأن التبسم قد لا يكون ضحكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It is the truth confirming” is not emphatic because being true in itself differs from confirming what preceded it.
rows.anchor: ولا ﴿ وهو الحق مصدقا ﴾ لاختلاف المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “who takes his desire as his god,” the default order is “his desire as his god”; the second object is fronted for emphasis.
rows.anchor: والأصل ( هواه إلهه ) لأن من اتخذ إلهه هواه غير مذموم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If “dark” means green, it describes the pasture; the order is changed for the verse ending.
rows.anchor: على تفسير ( أحوى ) بالأخضر وجعله نعتا للمرعى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expected order is “black, intensely black,” since gharabib already means intensely black; the order is reversed.
rows.anchor: والأصل ( سود غرابيب ) لأن الغربيب الشديد السواد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: She received the good news and then laughed, reversing the event order in the wording.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فضحكت فبشرناها ﴾ أي فبشرناها فضحكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “he would have desired her” absent the sight of his Lord’s proof; on this reading the actual intention is negated.
rows.anchor: أي لهم بها وعلى هذا فالهم منفي عنه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says speakers generally place first what matters more to explain and what they care more to explain.
rows.anchor: كما قال سيبويه في كتابه كأنهم يقدمون الذي بيانه أهم وهم ببيانه أعنى

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Saʾigh says fronting has ten specific purposes beyond the general principle of prioritizing what matters.
rows.anchor: قال هذه الحكمة إجمالية وأما تفاصيل أسباب التقديم وأسراره

words: شهد الله أنه لا إله إلا هو
rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: The first purpose is seeking blessing by placing God’s name first in important matters, as in the testimony of divine unity and distribution of spoils.
rows.anchor: الأول التبرك كتقديم اسم الله تعالى في الأمور ذات الشأن

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: The second purpose is glorification: God precedes the Messenger in “God and His angels send blessings,” “God and the Messenger,” and similar pairings.
rows.anchor: الثاني التعظيم كقوله ﴿ ومن يطع الله

rows.speaker: ابن الصائغ
rows.claim: The third purpose is honor: examples put men before women, the free before the enslaved, the living before the dead, and hearing before sight. Ibn ʿAtiyya reports al-Naqqash’s argument that this ordering favors hearing and sight.
rows.anchor: الثالث التشريف كتقديم الذكر على الأنثى نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When either element could be omitted, the second is usually omitted; examples include forms in which the second predicate or genitive is understood.
rows.anchor: إذا دار الأمر بين كون المحذوف أولا أو ثانيا فكونه ثانيا أولى

words: إن الله وملائكته يصلون على النبي
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exception requires omission of the first element: with the nominative reading of “His angels,” the plural predicate applies only to the second subject, so the first predicate is elided.
rows.anchor: وقد يجب كونه من الأول نحو

words: أن الله بريء من المشركين ورسوله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An exception requires omission of the second element: the earlier predicate “free” also applies to the later subject, His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وقد يجب كونه من الثاني نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A taḏyīl is a following sentence containing the first sentence’s meaning and confirming it, clarifying for those who missed it and consolidating for those who understood; this verse is an example.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يؤتى بجملة عقب جملة والثانية تشتمل على المعنى الأول لتأكيد منطوقه أو مفهومه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis may use inna, anna, lām, ala, amma, ha, ka-anna, lakin, layta, laʿalla, pronouns, qad, future markers, emphatic nuns and negative particles.
rows.anchor: وهي إن وأن ولام الابتداء والقسم وألا الاستفتاحية وأما وها التنبيه وكأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Emphasis is apt when the addressee doubts or denies; its strength varies with the intensity of denial.
rows.anchor: وإنما يحسن تأكيد الكلام بها إذا كان المخاطب به منكرا أو مترددا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the first denial, Jesus’s messengers use inna and a nominal sentence; after stronger denial they add an oath and lām as well.
rows.anchor: فأكد بأن وإسمية الجملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Someone acting against his admission may be treated as a denier; death is emphasized twice though not denied, while resurrection gets one emphasis despite stronger denial because its proofs are plain.
rows.anchor: وقد يؤكد بها والمخاطب به غير منكر لعدم جريه على مقتضى إقراره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “No doubt in it” categorically denies doubt although some people doubt; their doubt is treated as absent because compelling proofs should remove it.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قوله تعالى ﴿ لا ريب فيه ﴾

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says death is emphasized three times to keep it before people’s eyes, since worldly striving makes them behave as if they will live forever.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري بولغ في تأكيد الموت تنبيها للإنسان

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says resurrection is affirmed only with inna because it is presented as certainty admitting no dispute or denial.
rows.anchor: ولم يؤكد جملة البعث إلا بإن لأنه أبرز في صورة المقطوع به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet said a monkey’s hindquarters are not beautiful, but God fashioned its creation perfectly.
rows.anchor: أما إن است القردة ليست بحسنة ولكنه أحكم خلقها

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muʿadh ibn Jabal reports the Prophet glossed people’s sides withdrawing from beds as a servant’s night prayer.
rows.anchor: قال ( قيام العبد من الليل )

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet glossed the one made guidance for the Children of Israel as Moses.
rows.anchor: قال ( جعل موسى هدى لبني إسرائيل )

words: فلا تكن في مرية من لقائه
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet glossed the meeting as Moses meeting his Lord.
rows.anchor: قال ( من لقاء موسى ربه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An is explanatory after a sentence with a sense of saying and before another sentence; in 38:6 it means their tongues launch into speech, not that their bodies set out to walk.
rows.anchor: وأن يتأخر عنها جملة وأن يكون في الجملة السابقة معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs’ “go on” means persist in following the idols, not ordinary walking.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد المشي المتعارف بل الاستمرار على المشي

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari calls an explanatory here; the author rejects this because revelation to the bee is unanimously inspiration, not speech, so an is a verbal noun meaning “making.”
rows.anchor: وزعم الزمخشري أن التي في قوله

rows.speaker: ابن هشام
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari allows an to explain the command in “I only told them what You commanded me”; Ibn Hisham finds this plausible and refines the rule for explicit words of saying.
rows.anchor: قال ابن هشام وهو حسن وعلى هذا فيقال في الضابط

words: ما قلت لهم إلا ما أمرتني به
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the rule inconsistent: grammarians demand a sense of saying, yet reinterpret an explicit verb of saying as another act; he compares this with treating al in al-aan as redundant although it carries meaning.
rows.anchor: قلت وهذا من الغرائب كونهم يشرطون أن يكون فيها معنى القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Anas ibn al-Nadr is named among those who fulfilled their vow.
rows.anchor: سمي منهم أنس بن النضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel is named as the first to say the truth, after whom the others follow.
rows.anchor: أول من يقول جبريل فيتبعونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs are identified as ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt, Abu Jahl, al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib and al-Aswad ibn Yaʿuth.
rows.anchor: سمي منهم عقبة بن أبي معيط وأبو جهل

words: وقالوا ما لنا لا نرى رجالا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Jahl is named among the speakers asking why they do not see certain men; ʿAmmar and Bilal are among the men.
rows.anchor: سمي من القائلين أبو جهل ومن الرجال عمار وبلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The jinn group is named as Zawbaʿa, Hasi, Masi, Shasir, Masir, al-Urd, Inyan, al-Ahkam and Saraq.
rows.anchor: سمى منهم زوبعة وحسي ومسي وشاصر وماصر

words: إن الذين ينادونك من وراء الحجرات
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those calling the Prophet from behind the chambers are named as al-Aqraʿ ibn Habis, al-Zibriqan ibn Badr, ʿUyayna ibn Hisn and ʿAmr ibn al-Ahtam.
rows.anchor: سمي منهم الأقرع بن حابس والزبرقان بن بدر

words: ألم تر إلى الذين تولوا قوما
rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the verse concerns the hypocrite ʿAbd Allah ibn Nufayl.
rows.anchor: قال السدي نزلت في عبد الله بن نفيل من المنافقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed concerning Qutayla, mother of Asmaʾ bint Abi Bakr.
rows.anchor: نزلت في قتيلة أم أسماء بنت أبي بكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believing women are named as Umm Kulthum bint ʿUqba ibn Abi Muʿayt and Umayma bint Bishr.
rows.anchor: سمي منهم أم كلثوم بنت عقبة بن أبي معيط وأميمة بنت بشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy is named as the speaker of both “do not spend” and “if we return.”
rows.anchor: سمي منهم عبدالله بن أبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source names Israfil, Lubnan and Rufaʾil among the bearers of the Throne.
rows.anchor: سمي من حملة العرش إسرافيل ولبنان وروفيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the trench are identified as Dhu Nuwas, Zarʿa ibn Asad al-Himyari and their companions.
rows.anchor: ذو نواس وزرعة بن أسد الحميري وأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of the elephant were Abyssinians, led by Abraha al-Ashram and guided by Abu Righal.
rows.anchor: هم الحبشة قائدهم أبرهة الأشرم ودليلهم أبو رغال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah is said to have been revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, al-ʿAsi ibn Waʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Mutalib and Umayya ibn Khalaf.
rows.anchor: نزلت في الوليد بن المغيرة والعاصي بن وائل والأسود ابن المطلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source identifies the sorceresses who blow on knots as Labid ibn al-Aʿsam’s daughters.
rows.anchor: ﴿ النفاثات ﴾ بنات لبيد بن الأعصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says his cited work treats the remaining unnamed peoples, animals, places and times in detail.
rows.anchor: وأما مبهمات الأقوام والحيوانات والأمكنة والأزمنة ونحو ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says akwab means cups in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: أكواب حكى ابن الجوزي أنها الأكواز بالنبطية

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak says akwab means handleless jars in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: عن الضحاك أنها بالنبطية جرار ليست لها عرى

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni says il is reported to be God’s name in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جنى ذكروا أنه اسم الله تعالى بالنبطية

rows.speaker: ابن الجوزي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Jawzi says alim means painful in Zanjiyya.
rows.anchor: أليم حكى ابن الجوزي أنه الموجع بالزنجية

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla says alim means painful in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: وقال شيذلة بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla glosses inahu as ripening or cooking in Maghrebi speech.
rows.anchor: إناه نضجه بلسان أهل المغرب ذكره شيذلة

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim gives the gloss inahu in Berber.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو القاسم بلغة البربر

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla says hamim an and ʿayn aniya refer to water whose heat has reached its limit, that is, hot water.
rows.anchor: هو الذي انتهى حره بها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas, through ʿIkrima, glosses awwah as one who is certain in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال الأواه الموقن بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: مجاهد، عكرمة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Hatim reports the same Ethiopian gloss, “one who is certain,” from Mujahid and ʿIkrima.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد وعكرمة

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil says awwah means merciful in Ethiopian.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شرحبيل قال الرحيم بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: الواسطي
rows.claim: Al-Wasiti says awwah means supplication in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: وقال الواسطي الأواه الدعاء بالعبرية

rows.speaker: عمرو بن شرحبيل
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Shurahbil glosses awwab as one who praises God in Ethiopian, and glosses “praise with him” as “glorify” in that language.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن شرحبيل قال الأواب المسبح بلسان الحبشة

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla says al-milla al-akhira means the first pre-Islamic religion: Coptic calls “the latter” “the first,” and vice versa; al-Zarkashi cites this explanation.
rows.anchor: الملة الآخرة قال شيذلة الجاهلية الأولى أي الآخرة في الملة الآخرة

rows.speaker: شيذلة
rows.claim: Shidhla says brocade linings mean the outer surfaces are brocade in Coptic; al-Zarkashi cites this.
rows.anchor: أي ظواهرها بالقبطية وحكاه الزركشي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses a baʿir measure as the load of a donkey.
rows.anchor: ﴿ كيل بعير ﴾ أي كيل حمار

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says baʿir is any beast used to carry a load in Hebrew.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل إن البعير كل ما يحمل عليه بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: الجواليقي
rows.claim: Al-Jawaliqi says some scholars considered biʿa, a church, an Arabized Persian word.
rows.anchor: قال الجواليقي في كتاب المعرب البيعة والكنيسة جعلهما بعض العلماء

rows.speaker: الجواليقي والثعالبي
rows.claim: Al-Jawaliqi and al-Thaʿalibi say tannur is an Arabized Persian word.
rows.anchor: ذكروا الجواليقي والثعالبي أنه فارسي معرب

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr glosses tabtiran as destruction in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وليتبروا ما علوا تتبيرا ﴾ قال تبره بالنبطية

rows.speaker: أبو القاسم
rows.claim: Abu al-Qasim says “from beneath her” means “from her belly” in Nabataean.
rows.anchor: ﴿ فناداها من تحتها ﴾ أي بطنها بالنبطية

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
rows.claim: Ibn Abi al-Isbaʿ defines this device as naming a praised person’s forefathers in birth order and cites Joseph’s “religion of my fathers.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي الأصبع ومنه في القرآن قوله تعالى حكاية عن يوسف

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
rows.claim: Joseph does not use the customary order from father to grandfather; he names the religion’s founder first, then those who received it in sequence.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم يأت به على الترتيب المألوف فإن العادة الابتداء بالأب ثم الجد

rows.speaker: ابن أبي الإصبع
rows.claim: The sons of Jacob similarly mention their forefathers in the order of the religion they followed.
rows.anchor: ومثله قول أولاد يعقوب ﴿ نعبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People derived dream interpretation from Joseph’s dreams and prison companions’ visions; when the Quran did not resolve a case, they used explanatory Sunnah, sayings and proverbs, considering customary usage indicated by the command to observe recognized practice.
rows.anchor: واستنبط قوم مما فيه من أصول التعبير مثل ما ورد في قصة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others developed inheritance law and calculation from the inheritance verses, including shares, proportional adjustment and rulings on bequests.
rows.anchor: وأخذ قوم مما في آية المواريث من ذكر السهام وأربابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People derived timekeeping from verses about day and night, the sun and moon, their phases, stars and constellations.
rows.anchor: ونظر قوم إلى ما فيه من الآيات الدالات على الحكم الباهرة

rows.speaker: الكتاب والشعراء
rows.claim: Writers and poets derived semantics and rhetorical sciences from Quranic eloquence, arrangement, context, openings, endings, shifts of address, expansion and concision.
rows.anchor: ونظر الكتاب والشعراء إلى ما فيه من جزالة اللفظ وبديع النظم

rows.speaker: أرباب الإشارات وأصحاب الحقيقة
rows.claim: People of spiritual allusion and inner reality derived subtle senses and terms such as annihilation, abiding, presence, fear, awe, intimacy, estrangement, contraction and expansion.
rows.anchor: ونظر فيه أرباب الإشارات وأصحاب الحقيقة فلاح لهم من ألفاظه معان ودقائق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran encompasses older sciences; medicine maintains health through balance, summarized by moderation, and restores it through the drink with healing, while also treating hearts and breasts.
rows.anchor: أما الطب فمداره على حفظ نظام الصحة واستحكام القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lat means not the time of escape.
rows.anchor: 1927 ﴿ ولات حين مناص ﴾ ليس حين فرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilaq means fabrication.
rows.anchor: 1928 ﴿ اختلاق ﴾ تخريص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The routes mean the sky.
rows.anchor: 1929 ﴿ فليرتقوا في الأسباب ﴾ السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fuwaq means a return or repetition.
rows.anchor: 1930 ﴿ من فواق ﴾ ترداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their allotted portion is glossed as punishment.
rows.anchor: 1931 ﴿ عجل لنا قطنا ﴾ العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means he began wiping.
rows.anchor: 1932 ﴿ فطفق مسحا ﴾ جعل يمسح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jasad here means a devil.
rows.anchor: 1933 ﴿ جسدا ﴾ شيطانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rukhaʾ means compliant wherever he wished.
rows.anchor: 1934 ﴿ رخاء حيث أصاب ﴾ مطيعة له حيث أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dighth means a bundle.
rows.anchor: 1935 ﴿ ضغثا ﴾ حزمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people of hands are those with strength.
rows.anchor: 1936 ﴿ أولي الأيدي ﴾ القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Insight means understanding in religion.
rows.anchor: 1937 ﴿ والأبصار ﴾ الفقه في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who restrain their gaze do so from men other than their husbands.
rows.anchor: 1938 ﴿ قاصرات الطرف ﴾ عن غير أزواجهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atrāb means equal in age or status.
rows.anchor: 1939 ﴿ أتراب ﴾ مستويات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghassaq means bitter cold.
rows.anchor: 1940 ﴿ وغساق ﴾ الزمهرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Azwaj means varieties of punishment.
rows.anchor: 1941 ﴿ أزواج ﴾ ألوان من العذاب
